problem:
Let X be a connected compact complex manifold of dimension n, and use dd^c=(i/(2 pi)) partial barpartial. A smooth real (1,1)-background theta need not be closed. PSH(X,theta) consists of genuine quasi-plurisubharmonic u with theta+dd^c u>=0. Write v preceq u if v<=u+C for some constant C; ordinary equivalence means bounded difference. The multiplier ideal I(tu) consists of germs g for which |g|^2 exp(-tu) is locally integrable. Write v preceq_I u if I(tv) is contained in I(tu) for every real t>0. For a smooth real obstacle F define P_{theta,F}[u]=(sup{v in PSH(X,theta):v<=F, v preceq u})^* and P_{theta,F}[u]_I=(sup{v in PSH(X,theta):v<=F, v preceq_I u})^*, where * is upper semicontinuous regularization. Omitting F means F=0. For a positive Hermitian form h, bounded mass (BMP) means the supremum of integral_X(h+dd^c v)^n over bounded h-psh v is finite. The extended non-pluripolar measure MA_theta^ext(v) is the increasing finite-level product, which may have infinite total mass. The lower singularity volume of an ordinary type q is inf{MA_theta^ext(v)(X):v in PSH(X,theta),v equivalent to q}. The relative envelope class E_env(X,theta,q) consists of u preceq q such that for every b>=1 some v in PSH(X,theta) satisfies b^(-1)v+(1-b^(-1))q<=u; this uses convex sums even at common poles.

Question: suppose the smooth background theta is admissible for these envelope constructions, u belongs to PSH(X,theta), and P_theta[u]=P_theta[u]_I is genuine. Must P_{theta,F}[u]=P_{theta,F}[u]_I for every smooth real obstacle F, without positive lower ideal volume or BMP? Establish the implication in unrestricted higher-dimensional zero-volume and unbounded-mass settings, or give a counterexample. All-obstacle equality implies zero-obstacle equality by F=0. The converse is known when u belongs to E_env(X,theta,P_theta[u]_I), under BMP plus positive lower volume of the ideal envelope, on curves without volume restrictions, and in specified separated-product and divisorial-curve-fibration cases. These are background rather than resolutions of the unrestricted question. Smooth-gauge transport is also background.
completionCriteria: Prove the universal implication with all original hypotheses and without adding BMP or positive lower volume, or exhibit a compact complex manifold, explicit admissible smooth background theta, a genuine theta-psh u and a smooth obstacle F with rigorously proved zero-obstacle envelope equality and rigorously proved unequal obstacle envelopes. Expand any further admissibility used. A restricted example, a theorem repeating the known relative-envelope criterion, or gauge transport alone cannot resolve the question. Check all external premises against primary sources and reconstruct the complete proof independently.
